run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Investigated hotel-reservation after it was (re)deployed at 21:12-21:13Z, only 2-3 minutes before the end of the authorized window, so there is no pre-incident baseline for the application itself (earliest app/span metric samples are ~21:13-21:14Z). Facts: all application pods (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user, consul, jaeger, six mongodb pods, three memcached pods) are Running and Ready with 0 restarts except recommendation-86cf75495d-c9gmw, which restarted once at 21:13:10Z (exit code 2) after 'panic: no reachable servers' while mongodb-recommendation was still initializing; its current instance connected and registered in consul. Sampled traces show the request path complete and fast: HTTP GET /hotels spans 2.7-3.9ms with http.status_code=200, frontend->search->(geo, rate), frontend->reservation.CheckAvailability, frontend->profile->memcached, every span well under 10ms; span-counter deltas between 21:14:00Z and 21:15:00Z show caller and callee counts matching within about +-10, so no evidence of hung downstream RPCs. The rate and search services' own metrics are healthy over that minute (rate_requests_received/completed +3393 with rejected 0, expired 0, queue_depth 0, in_flight 0; search_rate_attempts +3391, successes +3390, failures 0, timeouts 0). The only client-visible anomaly is on the load generator: wrk2 rounds report 188-195 socket read timeouts per ~2933-2972 requests (about 6-7%) while successful requests are all <=10.08ms, and those timed-out requests have no server span, no HTTP error status, no application error log, and no node TCP retransmit/timeout or pod interface drop counter, so with the available telemetry they cannot be attributed to a named backend. Hypothesis-level finding: ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate contain scripts that revoke user 'admin' readWrite on geo-db/rate-db, and Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate were re-rolled at 21:12:40-41Z to new ReplicaSets that mount these ConfigMaps as a 'failure-script' volume at /scripts (image unchanged mongo:4.4.6); however no mongo authorization failure, no app error and no rate/search failure was observed, so the declared fault was not seen applied or effective in the sampled window. The recommendation restart and the NotReady audit-log-archiver CronJob pods (archiver container exited 0, fluent-bit sidecar still running) are separate, non-app-path changes; the persistent blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe failure is a monitoring artifact because no Ingress exists in the namespace. Because the fault's application cannot be observed, no root cause is named.

ConfigMaps named failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate exist in hotel-reservation and hold fault scripts: revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh / revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh downgrade mongo user 'admin' by revoking the readWrite role on geo-db / rate-db, alongside remove-admin-mongo.sh and revoke-mitigate-admin-*-mongo.sh restore scripts; mongo-geo-script / mongo-rate-script are the init scripts that create admin/root and grant readWrite.

The current ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 (created 21:12:41Z) mount an extra volume named 'failure-script' at /scripts in addition to the init-script volume, whereas the earlier ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf (created 21:12:37-38Z, now 0 replicas) mount only /data/db and /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d; the container image is unchanged (mongo:4.4.6), i.e. a configuration-only pod-template change on those two Deployments during the window.

Deployment events show the two rollouts during the window: 'Scaled down replica set mongodb-geo-78487c9767 from 1 to 0' at 21:12:40Z then 'Scaled up replica set mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 from 0 to 1' at 21:12:41Z, and 'Scaled down replica set mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf from 1 to 0' at 21:12:40Z then 'Scaled up replica set mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 from 0 to 1' at 21:12:41Z.

Alerts firing at query time: HighRequestRate for frontend, profile, rate, reservation and search (pending for geo) in namespace hotel-reservation, and KubePodNotReady for hotel-reservation pods audit-log-archiver-29924474-6q87q (firing) and audit-log-archiver-29924475-5t4c5 (pending); HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, DeploymentNotReady and PodStatusError are inactive.

The audit-log-archiver CronJob pods are NotReady because their archiver container ran to completion and exited 0 while the fluent-bit sidecar keeps running: audit-log-archiver-29924474-6q87q archiver terminated Completed at 21:14:04Z (log: 'archiver: audit record forwarded', 'upload complete (0 bytes archived)') with Ready=False and ContainersReady=False, sidecar fluent-bit-sidecar running.

The blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe to http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels returns probe_success 0 and probe_http_status_code 0 at 21:13:00/21:14:00/21:15:00Z, while no Ingress object exists in namespace hotel-reservation; by contrast every direct service probe (frontend:5000, geo:8083, profile:8081, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, reservation:8087, search:8082, user:8086) went from 0 to 1 as the pods started and stayed 1 (profile first succeeded at 21:14:15Z).

Against any downstream service failing: the only status_code value on traces_span_metrics_calls_total is STATUS_CODE_UNSET and the HTTP spans carry http.status_code=200; the only error-looking lines in the namespace over 21:10-21:15Z were the recommendation startup panic, wrk2 socket-timeout counters and benign mongo startup notices; the load generator reported connect 0 / read 0 / write 0 socket errors, i.e. no non-2xx responses.

Against the mongo admin-privilege revoke being in effect: rate's traced mongo reads continue at roughly the same miss ratio as the unauthenticated profile datastore - rate made 3436 /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans and 63 mongo_rate client spans while profile made 5685 /profile.Profile/GetProfiles server spans and 61 mongo_profile client spans between 21:14:00 and 21:15:00Z - and rate/search counters show 0 failures, so no denied-read pattern is visible.

Rejected: an elevated-latency incident in the traced services. The HighRequestLatency rule (p95 > 3000ms) is inactive, mean durations are sub-millisecond to ~5ms, and the bucket increases show 100% of frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' spans and 100% of search->rate spans below 10ms.

Rejected as impact: the single recommendation restart. Its previous instance exited 2 with 'panic: no reachable servers' 13s after start while mongodb-recommendation was still initializing, the replacement connected on the first retry at 21:13:11Z and the pod has been Ready since, and the trace counters show recommendation serving ~2255 requests/min with no failures.

The ~6-7% of load-generator requests that get no response are lost or stuck before the frontend HTTP handler creates a span: they produce no frontend server span (frontend HTTP span deltas match wrk2's completed-request count), no HTTP error status, no application log line, and no TCP-level retransmission/timeout or interface drop counter, so no backend can be named as their source from the available telemetry; frontend and its pod frontend-68745cb99c-gn4gn are where the loss becomes visible, but their own signals show no failure.

The ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, now mounted as the 'failure-script' volume into mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-x84cs and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-gmjsm, are the prepared fault payload for the geo-db and rate-db mongo 'admin' privileges (revoke readWrite), and the 21:12:40-41Z re-rolls of Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate are the mechanism that placed them; their declared effect (denied reads in geo/rate) was not observed in the sampled 21:14-21:15Z metrics, traces or mongo logs, so whether the revoke was ever executed is unknown.

Inspect the wrk2 Job's script/CLI (pod wrk2-job-kr9m9, target http://10.96.230.162:5000) to learn which paths it times out on, and add a server-side frontend metric or log (status class, in-flight count, read timeout) so requests that never produce a span become attributable.

Verify in the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate pods whether /scripts/revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or /scripts/revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh has been executed (e.g. db.getUser('admin').roles) and whether the matching revoke-mitigate-admin-*-mongo.sh must be applied; do not assume the fault is inactive just because the current counters are clean.

Fix the audit-log-archiver CronJob template so the fluent-bit sidecar exits after the archiver completes (or model completion explicitly), since its pods stay NotReady and keep KubePodNotReady firing; and point or remove the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe because namespace hotel-reservation has no Ingress to probe.

The ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, now mounted as the 'failure-script' volume into mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-x84cs and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-gmjsm, are the prepared fault payload for the geo-db and rate-db mongo 'admin' privileges (revoke readWrite), and the 21:12:40-41Z re-rolls of Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate are the mechanism that placed them; their declared effect (denied reads in geo/rate) was not observed in the sampled 21:14-21:15Z metrics, traces or mongo logs, so whether the revoke was ever executed is unknown.

recommendation.text: Inspect the wrk2 Job's script/CLI (pod wrk2-job-kr9m9, target http://10.96.230.162:5000) to learn which paths it times out on, and add a server-side frontend metric or log (status class, in-flight count, read timeout) so requests that never produce a span become attributable.

Verify in the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate pods whether /scripts/revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or /scripts/revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh has been executed (e.g. db.getUser('admin').roles) and whether the matching revoke-mitigate-admin-*-mongo.sh must be applied; do not assume the fault is inactive just because the current counters are clean.

Fix the audit-log-archiver CronJob template so the fluent-bit sidecar exits after the archiver completes (or model completion explicitly), since its pods stay NotReady and keep KubePodNotReady firing; and point or remove the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe because namespace hotel-reservation has no Ingress to probe.

counter_evidence.text: Against any downstream service failing: the only status_code value on traces_span_metrics_calls_total is STATUS_CODE_UNSET and the HTTP spans carry http.status_code=200; the only error-looking lines in the namespace over 21:10-21:15Z were the recommendation startup panic, wrk2 socket-timeout counters and benign mongo startup notices; the load generator reported connect 0 / read 0 / write 0 socket errors, i.e. no non-2xx responses.

Against the mongo admin-privilege revoke being in effect: rate's traced mongo reads continue at roughly the same miss ratio as the unauthenticated profile datastore - rate made 3436 /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans and 63 mongo_rate client spans while profile made 5685 /profile.Profile/GetProfiles server spans and 61 mongo_profile client spans between 21:14:00 and 21:15:00Z - and rate/search counters show 0 failures, so no denied-read pattern is visible.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: an elevated-latency incident in the traced services. The HighRequestLatency rule (p95 > 3000ms) is inactive, mean durations are sub-millisecond to ~5ms, and the bucket increases show 100% of frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' spans and 100% of search->rate spans below 10ms.

Rejected as impact: the single recommendation restart. Its previous instance exited 2 with 'panic: no reachable servers' 13s after start while mongodb-recommendation was still initializing, the replacement connected on the first retry at 21:13:11Z and the pod has been Ready since, and the trace counters show recommendation serving ~2255 requests/min with no failures.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \

data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

data.k8s-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
